rows.description: A teenager checks messages constantly, feels dread at delayed replies and may test the partner with jealousy. Wants closeness badly, and learning to self-soothe protects the relationship from overwhelm.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, jealousy, overwhelm

rows.description: A wise teenager learns to pause before sending a fourth text, name the fear and ask directly for what is needed. Building friendships, interests and self-worth outside one relationship lessens the pull.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, interest, calm

rows.subtype: Fear of abandonment in adult love [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult reads small cues as rejection, seeks reassurance and sometimes lashes out, then feels shame. Behind the intensity is a fear of being left, and it can soften with self-awareness and safe partners.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: affection, fear, shame, trust

rows.description: A partner of an anxious person feels watched and always needing to prove love, and may pull away, which confirms the fear. Warm consistency plus clear limits helps more than either giving in or withdrawing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: affection, fear, anxiety, detachment

rows.subtype: Toddler who does not seek comfort [Actor]
rows.description: A toddler seems unbothered when a caregiver leaves, plays alone and turns away when hurt. The calm can hide stress; the child has learned that showing need does not bring comfort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child insists on doing everything alone, hides tears and pulls away from hugs when upset. Independence looks strong, but the child may be guarding against disappointment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child says they do not care about being left out and buries feelings in games or screens. Learns that feelings are unwelcome, so adults need to invite them without pressure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teacher sees a child who never asks for help and looks fine during upsets. Quiet check-ins, choices instead of demands and steady availability let the child come closer in time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager pulls back once a friendship or relationship gets emotional, and prefers to handle problems alone. Closeness feels like a threat to freedom, and vulnerability is practised in small steps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult values freedom, avoids deep conversations and leaves when a partner asks for more. Inside there is often loneliness and fear of dependence, not a lack of feeling.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
